metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most of the questions are about specific parts of the output, and some could only come from reading it: 'Why this addition of generics?' (followed by 'I'm guessing the generics are implied rather than set anywhere'), 'Doesn't this need a new heading?', 'how is this possible if the schema is valid?' (asked about the quoted 'Missing lung side (528 records)' finding) and 'Only 1 flag for chestradqwen, despite the long list?'.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: Every applicable rule file (git, coding, python, the repo's CLAUDE.md) was in context, and the branch follows most of them: the commit subjects use the right Angular scopes, the feature release gets a minor bump (1.6.0 to 1.7.0, committed as `chore(datagen): bump version`), and the new public `CorrectionRules.flag` has a Google-style docstring. Compliance is still partial, because the rewritten docstrings for `Corpus.census`, `BatchOutputCorrector.correct_with_claude` and `DryRun.run` stretch their summaries over two lines, against the python rule that a docstring holds a one-line summary.
